title: Roos normalization of the tensor completion comparison
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a scheme $W$. Use the completed-coefficient categories, quotient completion $C_W$ and its actual unit $\eta_W$ of [def-sf-pull-completion-comparison]. Use an ordinary derived tensor presentation $T_W$ with its natural signed-total-tensor comparison on flat-term K-flat representatives [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and the actual completed tensor $\widehat T_W$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. A normalized tensor-completion presentation consists of this ordinary presentation, conversion of its good-representative certificates to those of the recorded integral operations, a natural isomorphism $C_W\circ T_W\simeq\widehat T_W$, and a natural chain map from the ordinary total tensor to the actual finite-tensor Roos complex. At every positive quotient and every homogeneous pure tensor $x\otimes y$, its first Roos coordinate is $(1\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$, and its shifted coordinate is zero. On every pair of good representatives, localization of this chain map is the ordinary tensor representative comparison followed by the actual completion unit, the preceding isomorphism, and the defining completed-tensor representative comparison. This is exactly the normalization of [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion]. Define $\chi:T_W\to\widehat T_W$ as $T_W\eta_W$ followed by that isomorphism; this specifies a comparison of the existing tensors, not a second tensor operation.
